cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a silk chapan coat embroidered with large sunburst rosettes in the suzani style, a form of dress and textile ornament used across northern/central Afghanistan and neighboring Central Asian groups; while this suzani embroidery is most associated with Uzbek/Tajik workshops rather than distinctively Hazara work, the chapan form is a plausible regional garment and neighboring ethnic traditions in this area cannot be reliably distinguished from imagery alone.

physical.title: coat (chapan)
physical.summary: Long sleeved coat (chapan) made up of a number of panels of beige coloured silk stitched together and embroidered with coloured silk thread. The embroiderered decoration consists of large rosettes in shades of  yellow, pink, red, brick orange and green surrounded by palmettes and floral sprays.  The coat has a small standing collar and is edged along the cuffs, hem and front opening with a narrow border with a repeat floral pattern in brick orange and green.  The coat is lined with a silk ikat fabric  in shades of blue, yellow, red, and black.
